content.about: Iran sits between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf, a land of high plateaus, deserts and snowy mountains. It is home to one of the world's oldest civilisations, and its cities hold blue-tiled mosques, gardens and bazaars. Persian poetry, carpets and saffron are famous worldwide. In ancient times, Iranians built underground channels called qanats to carry water across the desert.

standout.text: Persepolis, built about 2,500 years ago, was the ceremonial capital of the Persian Achaemenid Empire.

didYouKnow: Iran grows most of the world's saffron.
The game of polo has deep roots in ancient Persia.
Nowruz, the Persian New Year, begins on the first day of spring.
